ao-men-mian-zhi-niu-rou-fan.how: Cook the onion in a nonstick pan until the edges turn lightly golden. Add the ground beef and break it up promptly so the bits pick up a little browning. Add the sauce once the centre reaches 71°C (160°F). Stir the MSG into the sauce and add the starch slurry in several additions, keeping a thin, flowing glaze. Do not cook it long, or the meat turns hard. Taste before serving.
notes: canola or soybean oil, used with the reserved butter to cook the onion
stirred into the sauce to round out the meaty flavour

arancini.how: Brown the beef until it smells deeply browned. Fry the tomato paste until fragrant before adding the wine, and reduce the meat sauce until thick. Grate the cheese for the rice finely and mix it in while the rice is hot. Stir in the butter together with the added olive oil. Dice the filling cheese small and spread it evenly. Taste the meat sauce for salt once reduced, then chill.
notes: stirred into the rice to make up for the richness lost with less butter
dried thyme, added to the meat sauce with the tomatoes

bai-qie-ji.how: Use a small nonstick pan over medium-low heat. Cook the minced ginger first, then the green onion whites. Take the pan off the heat as soon as they smell fragrant and before they change colour. Stir in the sesame oil and the salt for the dip. Add a little of the poaching stock a spoonful at a time so the ginger-onion paste is moist but not thin. Taste for salt before serving. Chop the chicken into pieces with the skin on, and serve the dip in a separate dish.

bai-zhuo-xia.how: Sizzle the green onion, garlic and sesame seeds in hot oil first. Let it cool slightly, then stir in the light soy sauce, black vinegar, oyster sauce, MSG and white pepper so the sour, savoury and umami notes blend. Take the shrimp out as soon as they are cooked. Peel them and dip lightly, so the sauce clings directly to the meat and keeps its natural sweetness.
notes: added to the dipping sauce to round out the savoury flavour
added to the dipping sauce to add fragrance without covering the shrimp flavour

banh-mi-thit.how: Salt-rub, rinse and pickle in sweet-and-sour brine as in the original steps. Drain the pickles well before assembling. Stir the garlic paste into the mayonnaise and spread it thinly with the pâté over the cut sides. Slice the meat thin and lay it evenly, then sprinkle with black pepper, so every bite has meat, sweet-and-sour pickles and cilantro. Toast the bread until crisp and assemble just before eating.
notes: grated to a fine paste and stirred into the mayonnaise
freshly ground, sprinkled over the sliced meat

banh-xeo.how: For the filling, first fry the shallot and lemongrass until fragrant, then add the pork. Stir in the fish sauce and MSG just before it comes off the heat. Pat the shrimp dry and sear them in a hot pan until browned. For the dipping sauce, first mix the lime, sugar, garlic and chilies, then add the fish sauce and MSG. Eat with the thin, crisp pancake, lettuce and herbs.
notes: divided between the pork filling and the fish sauce dip to round out the savoury flavour
tender core only, minced very fine and cooked with the shallot until fragrant

bao-cai-chao-ji-dan-fen-si.how: Cook the green onion, garlic and dried chilies until fragrant, then add the drained shredded cabbage so it does not release water and thin the sauce. Loosen the glass noodles and toss them in the sauce. When the eggs go back in, drizzle the vinegar down the side of the pan. Toss, then taste. Add the reserved salt only if it needs it.
notes: drizzled down the side of the pan before serving, for fragrance without a sharp sourness
tossed into the sauce to round out the savoury flavour

bibim-guksu.how: Add the chili flakes and MSG to the sauce and stir well, so the sweet-and-sour, garlic and spicy notes blend. Rinse the noodles under cold water and drain well. Toss them right away with the sauce, sesame oil and green onion. Add the cucumber last so it does not release water and dilute the flavour.
notes: dissolved into the noodle sauce to round out the savoury flavour
finely sliced and tossed in with the noodles for a fresh note

bisque-de-homard.how: Soften the vegetables in olive oil and a little butter. Add the tomato paste and cook until fragrant, then add the lobster. Reduce the wine and extract the shell flavour as in the original steps. Cook the rice until very soft, then blend it with the base and strain again, using the rice starch to keep the soup thick and smooth. Off the heat, stir in the cream, then whisk in the remaining cold butter a little at a time. Taste for salt last. Only warm the lobster meat garnish through.
notes: choose a mild one, used to cook the vegetables
cooked down with the vegetables for umami and base flavour, without a tomato taste

blanquette-de-veau.how: Gently simmer the pearl onions, covered, in the cooking liquid, and add that liquid to the sauce. Cook a white roux with the butter and vegetable oil together, only until it bubbles and without browning. Temper the egg yolks and cream with a little hot sauce first, then return them to the pot. Heat gently to 74°C (165°F) and take it off the heat to keep the sauce silky. Before serving, season in stages with lemon juice and white pepper, then taste for salt.
notes: a neutral-tasting oil, used with the butter for the white roux to help the flour disperse evenly

boeuf-bourguignon.how: Fry the bacon until fragrant and remove it. Pour off the excess fat. Brown the beef in batches in the vegetable oil called for in the recipe, then deglaze with the red wine, scraping up the browned bits. Brown the pearl onions and mushrooms in the same vegetable oil. Keep the butter to stir in at the end. Skim the fat from the braising liquid and reduce it until it coats a spoon. Taste for salt before serving.

budae-jjigae.how: Render the bacon first, then soften the onion in the fat. Add the kimchi with its clinging juices and cook briefly. Arrange the other ingredients, then add the stock and seasoning paste. Cook the noodles separately and serve promptly after combining, so the broth does not reduce. Taste before serving. Brighten with rice vinegar, add the sesame oil off the heat, and add no more salt.
notes: use unsalted, unseasoned rice vinegar, added to taste at the end to brighten the kimchi
drizzled in off the heat to make up for the fat lost with less processed meat

bun-bo-hue.how: Clarify the shrimp paste as in the original and add it to the broth. Top up the broth, then stir in the MSG and keep it at a gentle simmer so it does not reduce. Still serve half of the chili lemongrass oil at the table. After filling the bowls, squeeze in lime and add fresh herbs. Taste first, then add the lemongrass oil, so the sour, spicy and savoury notes open up fully.
notes: added after the clarified shrimp paste goes in and the broth is topped up, to round out the savoury flavour

bun-bo-xao.how: Fry the lemongrass until fragrant. Sear the beef in batches, spread out, until browned, then add the fish sauce for the stir-fry. Stir the MSG into both the marinade and the sweet-and-sour dressing. After mixing the dressing, taste it with a piece of cucumber to balance sweet, sour and salty. Drain the vermicelli and vegetables well. Toss with the dressing and herbs before eating, tasting a full bite before adding more dressing.
notes: divided between the beef marinade and the fish sauce dressing to round out the savoury flavour
leaves only, tossed in before eating with the mint and cilantro

bun-cha.how: Stir the garlic paste into the original marinade. Shake off the extra marinade before grilling and brush the grill lightly with the oil from the marinade. Grill in batches, spread out, for browned, charred edges. Press the patties thin and do not press them while grilling. Take the patties and sliced pork off the heat when the centre reaches 71°C (160°F) to keep the juices in. Dissolve the MSG in the dipping sauce. Taste it with the meat, vermicelli and herbs together, and adjust until sweet, sour, salty and savoury are balanced.
notes: mashed to a paste, added to the marinade for the sliced pork and patties
dissolved in the fish sauce dip to round out the savoury flavour

bun-rieu.how: Keep all the salt for the crab-pounding step and add none to the broth. Use the fish sauce divided between frying the crab paste and seasoning the broth. Fry the shallots until fragrant and cook the chopped tomatoes until they release red oil, then add the crab broth. Stop stirring and let the crab curds form over low heat. Stir in the MSG off the heat. Add the rice vinegar in stages, tasting as you go. Top each bowl with cilantro and finish with lime and chili at the table.
notes: to round out the savoury flavour of the broth; use pure MSG
chopped, sprinkled over each bowl

bun-thit-nuong.how: Marinate the pork with the lemongrass, garlic and shallot. Drain off the excess liquid before grilling and grill spread out until browned on both sides. For the dressing, first dissolve the sugar and MSG in warm water, then stir in the lime juice, fish sauce and chilies. Taste it with the meat, noodles and vegetables to balance sweet and sour. Drain the noodles and vegetables well. Add the dressing a little at a time as you eat, so the grilled flavour, herbs and umami come through in every bite.
notes: tender core only, minced very fine and added to the marinade
dissolved in the dipping sauce to round out the savoury flavour

ca-ri-ga.how: Cook the lemongrass, green onion and garlic in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-low heat, stirring often. Add the chicken once the fragrance comes up. When the vegetables are nearly done, add the coconut milk and starch slurry. Stir gently and cook until the sauce thickens slightly, without a hard boil or letting it dry out. Add the fish sauce, sugar and MSG last, and taste the sauce with the chicken and potatoes together for salt.
notes: mixed with a little cold water to bring back the richness of the sauce, keeping it flowing
added before serving to support the savoury flavour of the chicken

carbonara.how: Cut the guanciale into small strips. Fry over medium heat, slowly, until the edges are golden and crisp. Keep the rendered fat so the pork flavour spreads evenly. Emulsify the fat in the pan with the pasta water. Off the heat, stir in the egg yolk and cheese paste. Toss the crisp meat back in last, and finish with freshly ground black pepper.

cassoulet.how: In step 3, brown the lamb in batches in a heavy-bottomed pot and turn it only once the surface is browned. After cooking the onion and tomato paste until fragrant, deglaze with hot bean broth, scraping up the browned bits. In step 6, keep plenty of liquid between the beans and bake until a thin crisp crust forms. Reduce the liquid, then taste for salt, so the meat, bean and garlic sausage flavours blend into the sauce.
notes: a neutral-tasting oil, used with the lard to brown the lamb
added after the onion and cooked until fragrant, before the tomato purée in the recipe

chang-fen.how: Cook the onion, garlic and shiitake until the edges are lightly golden. Add the green onion whites and water, cover and simmer until fragrant. Add the seasonings and MSG, bring to a boil, then strain. Sprinkle the rolled rice noodles with the green onion tops. While hot, pour the soy sauce mixture evenly over each roll so the thin rice sheets soak it up.
notes: added to the soy sauce mixture to round out the savoury flavour
whites crushed to cook in the sauce; tops thinly sliced and sprinkled on at the end

chao-ga.how: Top up the reduced chicken stock with water when starting the congee, and cook the ginger slices and green onion whites with the chicken thighs for flavour. For the dip, first let the ginger, lime and sugar blend, then stir in the fish sauce and let it rest. Dip the chicken in it as you eat. When the congee is cooked, stir in the MSG and salt. Top each bowl with white pepper, green onion tops and cilantro.
notes: stirred into the congee before serving to round out the savoury flavour
sprinkled over each bowl for fragrance

chao-he-fen.how: Use a nonstick pan. Drain the vegetables well, and cook the shredded meat and eggs separately, then set them aside. Soften and separate the rice noodles first so you do not need extra oil to keep them from sticking. Cook the green onion whites, garlic and cumin over low heat until fragrant, then add the noodles. Toss with the soy sauce, then add the vegetables back in. Stir-fry briefly until hot, with no liquid pooling. Taste for salt before serving and toss in the green onion tops.

chao-nian-gao.how: Use a nonstick pan. First cook the green onion whites in part of the oil over low heat until light golden, then remove them with the oil. Cook the eggs and vegetables in the remaining oil. Add the rice cakes, cooked soft and drained. If they stick, add a little hot water and gently push them loose. Toss with the light soy sauce until it just coats the rice cakes, then turn off the heat. Off the heat, stir the green onion oil and whites back in and sprinkle with the green onion tops. Taste before deciding whether to add salt.

che-chuoi.how: When cooking the coconut milk, top it up with water to the original volume and add the knotted pandan leaves. Heat gently and keep the step of steeping the sago, so the fragrance blends into the soup. Stop cooking when the bananas are soft and remove the leaf knot. Divide among bowls and sprinkle with crushed peanuts and toasted sesame seeds, keeping the coconut and nut flavours.
notes: pandan leaf, washed and tied in a knot, removed after cooking

com-ga-hoi-an.how: In step 4, use a nonstick heavy-bottomed pot. Cook the shallot over low heat until fragrant, then add the rice and turmeric and stir. Pour in hot chicken stock to cook the rice. In step 7, first toss the shredded chicken with lime juice and pepper. Let it rest, then taste for salt. Stir in the Vietnamese coriander before plating to keep the sour and fresh flavours.
notes: finely minced, cooked until fragrant before cooking the rice

com-tam-suon-nuong.how: Mix the lemongrass, garlic and green onion whites well into the marinade. Drain off the extra liquid before grilling. Grill first for browning, then move to a cooler spot to cook through. After mixing the fish sauce dressing, taste it with a piece of cucumber and adjust the finish with lime and chili. Sprinkle with cilantro on the plate and add the dressing a little at a time.
notes: divided between the pork chop marinade and the fish sauce dressing to round out the savoury flavour
chopped, sprinkled over the chops and rice on the plate

cong-you-ji.how: Cook the green onion whites in a small, narrow pot over low heat, stirring often. Turn off the heat when the edges turn light brown, then add the green onion tops and minced ginger to sizzle in the residual heat. Still use half of the ginger-green onion oil. Skim the fat off the stock and drain the chicken well. Stir the ginger-green onion oil, light soy sauce and stock together and toss in a little at a time, so the aromatic oil coats the pieces evenly.

coq-au-vin.how: Render the bacon first, then brown the chicken in batches. Brown the onion and mushrooms well in a nonstick pan. After adding the red wine, scrape up the browned bits. To thicken, knead the butter, the reserved vegetable oil and the flour together. Whisk it a little at a time into the braising liquid, which has been skimmed and reduced. Simmer gently until the raw flour taste is gone. Taste last and add salt and black pepper.
notes: a neutral vegetable oil; reserve 1 tsp to knead with the butter and flour for thickening, and split the rest between browning the chicken and cooking the mushrooms

creme-brulee.how: Warm the cream and take it off the heat. Stir in the salt and vanilla extract, then mix it into the egg yolk and sugar a little at a time. Strain and divide among shallow ramekins. Check the custards early while baking in a water bath. Take them out when the centre reaches 74°C (165°F) and still wobbles slightly as a whole. Chill completely and blot the surface dry. Sprinkle a thin layer of sugar and torch it to amber. Serve right away, once the sugar crust turns crisp.
notes: to bring out the cream, vanilla and caramel sweetness

crepes.how: Stir the warm butter and vegetable oil into the batter. Keep the chilling and resting step so the crepes are thin and soft. Brush a nonstick pan lightly with butter and cook over medium heat until light brown spots appear, without letting it turn bitter. Stack the crepes and cover them after cooking. Sprinkle with sugar while still warm and serve.
notes: a light canola oil, added to the batter to keep the crepes soft
added to the liquid with the rum, for a sweet-crepe aroma

dakbokkeumtang.how: Remove the skin from the chicken and trim off all visible fat, but braise with the bones in. Skim the fat during simmering and use the starch released by the potatoes to thicken the sauce, keeping it flowing. Toast the sesame seeds lightly until fragrant and stir them in with the sesame oil just before turning off the heat. Spoon the sauce over the chicken so the sweet, spicy sauce and sesame flavour cling to it.

dakjuk.how: Top up the stock to the original amount with hot water when cooking the chicken. After removing the chicken, keep the stock for the congee. Fry the rice in sesame oil until it smells of sesame, then add the stock. Return the shredded cooked chicken last. Stir in the MSG before serving, then season with the reserved salt, keeping the fragrance of the green onion and black pepper.
notes: stirred in before serving to round out the savoury flavour of the chicken and shiitake

dan-dan-mian.how: Dry-fry the ground pork first until the edges brown slightly. Then add the minced ginger and preserved mustard greens (ya cai) and cook until fragrant, so the topping stays dry and savoury. Dissolve the MSG in the warm water for the sauce. Smooth out the sesame paste, then mix in the other bowl seasonings. Toss the hot noodles well, so the vinegar, garlic, Sichuan pepper and chili oil coat them.
notes: total for two servings, dissolved in the bowl sauce to round out the flavour; use pure MSG, not salted chicken bouillon

dong-an-zi-ji.how: Use a nonstick pan. Cook the shredded ginger and chilies over medium-low heat until fragrant, then add the skin-on chicken and stir-fry so the skin renders a little fat. If the pan gets dry, add a little of the reserved stock. Add the rice vinegar in two parts: some when the chicken goes back in, and the rest once the chicken is cooked through and the thin sauce has reduced. Taste for salt, then toss in the green onion tops and sesame oil.
notes: added with the stock to round out the savoury flavour

dong-gua-sang-na-ji.how: Add the white pepper when marinating the chicken, mix well and chill, so the ginger and the seasoning coat the pieces. When arranging the plate, pour the marinade evenly over it. Spread the chicken in a single layer and take it out when the centre reaches 74°C (165°F). Sprinkle with green onion, and eat with the juices from the bottom of the plate. Taste before adding any more salt.
notes: sliced, sprinkled on after cooking
added when marinating the chicken, for fragrance without taking over

dou-ban-yu.how: Dry the fish well after marinating and pan-fry it until the skin is light golden. Cook the doubanjiang over medium-low heat until it releases red oil, then add the fermented black beans, ginger, garlic and green onion whites and cook until fragrant. Remove the fish once cooked. Reduce the red sauce separately until it thinly coats the back of a spoon. Add the MSG and vinegar near the end, stir in the green onion tops, and pour over the fish.
notes: added down the side of the pan near the end of the reduction, to add fragrance and cut richness without tasting sharply sour
dissolved into the red sauce after the fish is removed, to round out the savoury flavour

dou-chi-ling-yu-you-mai-cai.how: Cook the ginger and garlic over low heat in a little oil from the can. Crush the fermented black beans slightly and cook briefly until fragrant, so the salty, savoury flavour spreads evenly. Cook the lettuce until soft and drain off the liquid, then return it to the pan and toss quickly with the fish. Sprinkle with white pepper before serving. When tasting, take fish, black beans and greens together.
notes: minced, cooked with the garlic until fragrant
added before serving, for fragrance without covering the black bean flavour

dou-fu-nao.how: Cook the dried ingredients and green onion whites until fragrant before adding the liquid. Use the strained soaking water from the shiitake and lily buds for the sauce. Once the egg ribbons are cooked, stir in the MSG. Before serving, sprinkle with white pepper and green onion tops. Taste the tofu pudding together with the sauce, and finish with umami and fragrance rather than extra salt.
notes: added after the egg ribbons are cooked, to round out the savoury flavour of the sauce
added before serving, for fragrance

dou-jiao-men-mian.how: Use a nonstick pan. First cook the sliced pork until the edges turn lightly golden and a little fat renders. Add the green onion and ginger and cook until fragrant, then add the cooking wine and light soy sauce for aroma. Cook the green beans through before laying the noodles on top. Keep some liquid in the bottom of the pan and add the braising sauce a little at a time, so the noodles do not stick with less oil. Stir in the garlic when the noodles are cooked, and taste for salt before serving.
notes: drizzled down the side of the pan after the pork is fragrant; cook until the alcohol smell fades before adding water

egg-fried-rice.how: Use a nonstick pan. Divide the oil between cooking the eggs and the rice. Take out the eggs as soon as they set. Stir-fry the surface-dry rice in batches until separate and hot, then return the eggs and toss. Drizzle the light soy sauce down the side of the pan and toss. Finally add the green onion and white pepper, toss until fragrant and serve. Do not add more oil.
notes: sprinkled in before serving, for fragrance without covering the egg and green onion flavour

fettuccine-al-burro.how: Lift the hot pasta into a warmed large bowl. Toss with the olive oil first, then sprinkle in the finely grated cheese a little at a time. Alternate with warm pasta water and toss quickly. Finally add the softened butter and toss off the heat until the sauce thinly coats the pasta, keeping the butter flavour. Serve right away on warm plates.
notes: a mild one with no pronounced bitterness or pepperiness, to make up for the silkiness of the sauce

flammekueche.how: Start the bacon in a cold pan and cook over medium heat until the edges are lightly golden but still soft. Drain the fat and scatter the bacon, so every slice of tart has smoky, salty flavour. Mix the nutmeg and freshly ground black pepper into the cream and spread it thinly. Bake on a well-preheated baking sheet for a crisp base. Sprinkle with chives when it comes out.
notes: finely sliced, sprinkled on after baking for a fresh onion flavour

french-omelette.how: Use a small nonstick pan. Coat it with the vegetable oil first, then add part of the butter. When the butter foams but has not browned, add the eggs and stir quickly right away. Take the pan off the heat when the bottom layer sets and roll up the omelette. After plating, spread the reserved butter thinly over the hot omelette so the butter flavour stands out.
notes: a neutral vegetable oil, to add slipperiness while keeping the egg and butter flavour

frittata.how: Grate the cheese finely. Mix most of it into the eggs and save a little to sprinkle on the top before it goes under the broiler, so the cheese flavour stands out. Gently heat the butter and olive oil together to coat the bottom of the pan, then add the eggs and turn the heat to low. Take it out when the centre reaches 74°C (165°F) and move it off the hot pan, to keep it tender and buttery.
notes: used with the butter to coat the pan, adding a fruity note and helping prevent sticking

fu-qi-fei-pian.how: Chill the reserved braising liquid and skim off the fat. Heat it again to soak the chili flakes, then cool. Take half of the red oil and half of the moist chili sediment from the bottom. Mix with the prepared soy sauce, vinegar, Sichuan pepper powder, garlic, ginger and MSG. Toss with the thin slices of meat, taste and add salt. Sprinkle on the peanuts just before serving.
notes: a chili flake that is fragrant but not very hot, soaked in the hot defatted braising liquid to replace the chili aroma lost with less red oil
added to the dressing to round out the savoury flavour, so the lower-oil sauce still tastes rich

ga-kho-gung.how: Cook the caramel to a deep amber. Add the chicken, ginger, green onion and garlic and stir-fry until fragrant. Keep a little of the fish sauce to stir in just before serving, to keep its savoury aroma. When the chicken is cooked and tender, remove it first. Reduce the sauce on its own until it thinly coats the back of a spoon, then return the chicken to coat. Do not reduce too long, or the saltiness concentrates.
notes: stirred into the marinade to round out the savoury flavour

gaeng-garee-gai.how: Fry the curry paste in the vegetable oil and a little coconut milk until richly fragrant, then add the other liquids. Simmer gently in a small pot, covered, and add the potatoes later. When cooked through, stir in the starch slurry and simmer gently until the sauce thinly coats the potatoes. Before serving, adjust the salty, savoury, sweet and sour notes with the fish sauce, sugar and tamarind juice.
notes: an oil with no pronounced smell, to help bring out the aroma of the curry paste
mixed with the cold water set aside in the recipe and added last to thicken, for a sauce that coats

gaeng-keow-wan-gai.how: First cook the coconut cream, oil and curry paste until the raw smell fades and the fragrance builds. Then add the coconut milk, lemongrass and makrut lime leaves and simmer over low heat. Do not let it reduce on high heat. Add the reserved water only a little at a time if the main ingredients are not covered. Taste before serving and add fish sauce. Stir in the basil off the heat to keep the salty, savoury flavour, the heat and the clear herb aroma.
notes: tender sections, bruised and simmered for fragrance, removed before serving
leaves torn open and added with the coconut milk, removed before serving

gaeng-massaman.how: Fry the curry paste in the oil until fragrant, then add the thick coconut cream and stir. Do not wait for a lot of oil to separate before adding the meat. Simmer the beef until tender, then stir in the loosened peanut butter. Add the potatoes, then the starch slurry in stages, and simmer gently until the sauce thinly coats the back of a spoon. Before serving, taste the sauce and adjust the sweet, salty and sour notes with the tamarind, sugar and fish sauce already in the recipe.
notes: unsalted, unsweetened and smooth; loosen with hot liquid from the pot after the beef is tender, then stir in, for nutty richness
mixed with a little cold water and added in stages for the thickness you want

gaeng-phed-moo.how: First cook the curry paste in the thick coconut cream from the top and the vegetable oil until richly fragrant and oil droplets appear at the edges. Then add the sliced pork and the rest of the coconut milk, topping up with water to keep the volume. Add the lemongrass with the eggplant and cook until fragrant, then remove it. Just before serving, add the starch slurry as needed and cook briefly to thicken slightly. Taste and add fish sauce. Stir in the basil off the heat to keep it fresh.
notes: remove the dry, tough outer layers, then bruise and cut into large pieces; cook with the eggplant for fragrance and remove before eating, as it is not eaten
mixed with a little cold water and added just before serving as needed, to thicken the sauce slightly while keeping it flowing

gai-tod-hat-yai.how: Marinate the chicken legs and drain. Roast them on a rack until 79°C (175°F) near the bone, and discard the rendered fat. In a small nonstick pan, fry the shallots until crisp and keep the shallot oil. Mix the rice flour and the reserved water into a thin, drippy batter. Brush it on the chicken legs, with no batter pooling in the creases. Heat the shallot oil to 175°C (350°F). Fry the legs in batches, turning and spooning hot oil over them so the thin batter sets quickly. Drain on a rack once crisp and sprinkle with the fried shallots.

gan-bian-zi-ji.how: For the sauce, first cook the ginger and garlic over low heat until fragrant, then add the doubanjiang and cook until it releases red oil. Add the chili flakes and cook briefly, then add the sugar, Sichuan pepper and water right away. Reduce the sauce until thick first, then pour it over the fried chicken, potatoes and green peppers and toss quickly, so the sweet, spicy, savoury sauce coats the surface.
notes: cut into thin slices and cooked with the garlic until fragrant
to make up for the heat and Sichuan pepper aroma lost with less doubanjiang

gan-guo-hua-cai.how: Use a nonstick pan lightly coated with oil. Spread the sliced pork first and cook over medium heat until the edges are golden. Then add the garlic, chilies and fermented black beans and cook until fragrant. Blanch the cauliflower and drain it well. Return it to the pan over high heat and stir-fry, drizzling the light soy sauce down the side of the pan. Cook until the surface browns and no liquid pools at the bottom. Taste for salt before serving, then decide whether to add any.
notes: roughly chopped, for fermented bean flavour and umami; it is already salty, so add the salt for stir-frying last, if at all

goong-ob-woonsen.how: Heat the ginger, garlic, cilantro stems and pepper in the oil until clearly fragrant but the garlic is still pale. Then add the glass noodles and the braising sauce. Use unsalted chicken stock. Braise until the noodles absorb the sauce and nothing pools in the pan, then turn off the heat. Finally add the green onion, cover and let it steam, so the umami and aroma gather in the noodles.
notes: dissolved in the braising sauce to make up for the savoury flavour lost with less soy sauce and oyster sauce

gui-zhou-la-zi-ji.how: Remove the fat from the cavity and some of the thick skin from the chicken. Pan-fry in batches in a nonstick pan until light golden and pour off the rendered fat. Steam the potatoes until half-cooked, then pan-fry until fragrant. Leave a little oil in the pan. Slowly cook the zici chili, doubanjiang and ginger over medium-low heat, adding a little water if they stick. Cook until red and cooked-smelling, then braise in the original order. Finally uncover and reduce until the chili sauce coats the meat, then add the fermented rice and garlic shoots. Taste before adjusting the saltiness.

hachis-parmentier.how: Cook the onion, shallot and garlic in olive oil over medium-low heat until completely soft. Taste for salt before mixing in the meat. Soak the bread in the milk and stock and squeeze only lightly. Drain the potatoes and return them to the pot to steam off the water. Mash by hand and mix in the warm milk-stock mixture a little at a time. Finally stir in the butter to keep the dairy flavour. Sprinkle with a thin layer of breadcrumbs and bake until golden.
notes: used for cooking the aromatic vegetables and lightly oiling the baking dish, to make up for the richness lost with less butter
low-sodium and skimmed of fat, divided between the bread soaking liquid and the mashed potatoes to replace the reduced milk

haemul-pajeon.how: First mix the garlic, Korean chili flakes, vinegar and soy sauce and let it rest so the flavours blend. Pat the seafood dry before adding it to the batter. Spread the pancake thin and cook until golden on both sides, the green onion is fragrant and the centre is cooked through. Dip lightly just before eating, so the sour and savoury flavour sits on the surface.
notes: minced, added to the dipping sauce
added to the dipping sauce for mild heat and fragrance

he-lan-dou-chao-la-chang.how: Slice the Chinese sausage thin and cook over low heat until the edges curl slightly and the fat turns clear. Then add the ginger and garlic and cook until fragrant, without burning. Blanch the snow peas and drain them thoroughly. Stir-fry briefly over medium-high heat so the sweet, salty flavour and fat of the sausage coat the pods. Toss, taste and serve once hot.
notes: thinly sliced, for more garlic flavour
cut into fine shreds, for fragrance

he-nan-zheng-mian-tiao.how: Pat the sliced meat dry and spread it in a nonstick pan. Cook over medium heat until the edges are lightly golden. Use the rendered fat to cook the green onion, ginger and garlic until fragrant. Scrape up the browned bits when adding water. Add the white pepper to the vegetable broth. Toss it in with the noodles in stages, spread them loosely and steam again. Stir in the sesame oil off the heat, so the meat flavour and seasoning coat the noodles evenly.
notes: added once the vegetable broth is cooked, for fragrance without covering the meat flavour

hong-shao-li-yu.how: Cook the pork belly until the edges are lightly golden. Then cook the green onion, ginger, garlic and chilies until fragrant, and add the wine and vinegar down the side of the pan. Remove the fish when cooked. Reduce the sauce on its own until it coats a spoon, keeping the vinegar aroma and not reducing it too dry. Finally add the MSG, white pepper and garlic. Cook briefly, taste, and pour over the fish.
notes: added after the sauce is reduced, to round out the savoury flavour
added with the garlic before serving, for fragrance

hong-you-chao-shou.how: Dry-toast the chili flakes over low heat until fragrant, without burning. Mix them with the garlic paste, Sichuan pepper powder and the other bowl seasonings. Dissolve the MSG in a little hot cooking water and add. Stir up the fine sediment in the chili oil before scooping. Drain the wontons of visible drips, toss them in the sauce while hot, and sprinkle with green onion tops.
notes: a fine chili flake that is fragrant but not very hot, to add Sichuan chili aroma
added to the bowl sauce to round out the savoury flavour

hoy-lai-pad-nam-prik-pao.how: Use a deep nonstick pan. Cook the garlic over medium heat until fragrant, then add the chili paste and fry briefly. If the paste starts to stick, drizzle a little water down the side of the pan to loosen it. Right away add the clams and sliced chilies, cover and steam until they open. Uncover and mix the paste with the clam juices. Taste the cooked juices before deciding whether to add fish sauce. Finally stir in the basil and serve right away, keeping a thin sauce and not reducing it dry.

hu-la-tang.how: Keep the beef at a low simmer, covered, so the flavour of the beef and spices blends into the broth. In step 8, loosen the pepper, five-spice powder and MSG with hot broth. Return it to the pot, taste, and only then add salt. Stir in the sesame oil off the heat. Still add the vinegar to each bowl, to keep the spiciness and sour aroma.
notes: stirred in before serving with the light soy sauce, to round out the savoury flavour

janchi-guksu.how: Clean the anchovies of all guts and simmer them gently with the kombu to extract the umami, then strain. Add the soup soy sauce and MSG. Cook the shiitake until fragrant first, then the carrot, and season with black pepper. Cook the noodles in a separate pot, rinse them and reheat in boiling broth. Sprinkle with green onion in each bowl.
notes: added to the strained clear broth to boost the umami of the anchovies and kombu
finely sliced, sprinkled over each bowl

japchae.how: Use a nonstick pan to cook the egg sheets, brushing the pan lightly with oil. Still cook the vegetables in batches. Cook the mushrooms first to drive off water and then until fragrant. Cook the carrot in the leftover oil and add a little water if it sticks. Drain the glass noodles and toss them while hot with the soy sauce and sugar, then mix with the vegetables right away. Toss a little sesame oil with the spinach. Keep the rest to stir in last with the garlic and toasted sesame seeds, to preserve the aroma.

ji-cai-da-hun-tun.how: Keep the ground meat cold. First mix it with the salt for the filling, ginger paste, wine and pepper until sticky, then mix in the squeezed-dry shepherd's purse and sesame oil. For the broth, use unsalted chicken stock and stir in the MSG after heating. Just before serving, add the broth with sesame oil, pepper and green onion, and no extra salt. Divide the wontons and broth evenly among six bowls.
notes: grated to a fine paste and mixed into the filling, for fragrance without covering the shepherd's purse
added to the hot chicken stock to round out the savoury flavour

ji-dan-guan-bing.how: Mix the oil paste and spread it in a thin, continuous layer inside the dough. Keep the seam clean and roll lightly so the dough does not tear. Preheat a nonstick pan. Divide the pan-frying oil between both sides of the four pancakes, brush evenly and cook until golden spots form. Pour in the egg, cover and steam until cooked. At the end, uncover and cook briefly to bring back the crispness. Spread with sauce and add vegetables while hot.
notes: mixed into the green onion egg for the four pancakes, for fragrance

jian-jiao-chao-niu-rou.how: Mix the starch and white pepper into the beef when marinating. In a nonstick pan, first stir-fry the long hot peppers until slightly wrinkled and remove them. Then stir-fry the beef in batches, spread out and quickly. When the beef is nearly done, add the garlic and green onion and cook until fragrant, then return the peppers. Add a little of the marinade and cook through. Taste for salt before serving and plate as soon as the beef is cooked.
notes: mixed in when marinating the meat, forming a thin coating that helps the slices hold moisture and stay tender
added to the marinade to bring out the beef flavour without covering the pepper flavour

jiang-chao-ji.how: Use a nonstick pan. Cook the ginger slices over medium heat until fragrant and push them to the side. Cook the drained chicken in batches, spread out, until fragrant, then combine. Use the rendered chicken fat to cook the garlic, chilies and pickled chilies until fragrant. Add the beer and marinade, scrape up the browned bits and braise until the thickest part reaches 74°C (165°F). Reduce to a thin sauce that coats the chicken, then taste and add salt before serving.

jiang-cong-lao-ji.how: Drain the ginger and green onion and put them in a small pot. Stir them in hot oil over low heat until fragrant, keeping them pale to avoid bitterness. Skim the fat from the steaming juices from the chicken and stir a little into the ginger-green onion mixture. Then toss it with the coarsely shredded chicken, so the juices add savoury flavour and moisture. Finally taste and add salt.

jiang-dun-xie.how: Cook the ginger and garlic over medium-low heat first, then break up the soybean paste. When you smell the paste, add the dark soy sauce and cooking wine. Steam the crab pieces cut side down until cooked, keeping the crab juices. After steaming, stir the vinegar into the sauce at the bottom of the plate. Spoon it over the cut sides and dip as you eat.
notes: minced, cooked with the ginger until fragrant
stirred into the sauce at the bottom of the plate after cooking, to lift the flavour without a sour taste

jiang-pai-gu.how: Use a small nonstick pan. When making the caramel, add a little water to help dissolve the sugar. Once the water evaporates and the caramel turns light amber, add the dried ribs and toss. After mixing in the garlic and spices, add hot water promptly and simmer gently until tender. Then uncover and reduce until the sauce thinly coats the meat, so the caramel, meat and soy flavours gather on the surface of the ribs.

jiao-yan-pai-tiao.how: Add the white pepper when marinating the pork, and work in the green onion-ginger water in stages. Save part of the pepper salt for serving. Toast the green Sichuan peppercorns over low heat and grind fine. Mix them with the remaining white pepper and the pepper salt. Sprinkle the hot, drained fried pork strips lightly. Taste one strip first and then sprinkle on more, so the salty flavour gathers on the crisp crust.
notes: half for marinating the meat, and half mixed into the pepper salt for serving
unsalted dried green Sichuan peppercorns, toasted over low heat, ground fine and mixed into the pepper salt for serving

jie-mo-huang-you-luo-shi-xia.how: Pat the shrimp dry and sear until browned. Remove them, cook the garlic over low heat until fragrant, then return the shrimp to coat in the butter and sauce. Keep part of the wasabi to stir in at the end, to keep its pungency. When the sauce just coats the shells, add the rice vinegar and cilantro. Taste and serve right away. Do not reduce it to a dry sauce.
notes: stirred into the sauce to round out the savoury flavour
added before serving, to lift the flavour and cut richness

jie-mo-luo-shi-xia.how: Pat the shrimp shells and slits dry. Sear in a nonstick pan in a single layer, in batches if crowded. Add the garlic later. Add the bowl sauce without the wasabi as soon as the butter melts and cover briefly. Turn off the heat when the shrimp are cooked and the sauce coats the shells. Loosen the wasabi with a little sauce from the pan and stir it back in, to keep its sharp pungency. Taste for salt before serving.

jin-qian-dan.how: Cook the egg slices first until the edges are golden. Cook the chilies, garlic and doubanjiang in an empty spot in the pan until fragrant. Pour in the sauce and gently toss to lift, so the flavour coats the surface. Before serving, drizzle the vinegar down the side of the pan, then sprinkle with green onion and turn off the heat, keeping the sour and green onion aroma.
notes: drizzled down the side of the pan before serving, for aroma and flavour without an obvious sour taste
stirred into the sauce to make up for the savoury flavour lost with less sauce

jiu-cai-he-zi.how: Pat the shrimp dry and cook them through. Cook the crumbled eggs until fragrant. Once cool, mix with the garlic chives and sesame oil. Stir in the salt, MSG and white pepper just before filling. Pan-fry the pockets until golden on both sides, then uncover at the end to let steam escape, so the browned flavour stands out.
notes: to round out the savoury flavour of the shrimp and egg, mixed evenly into the filling just before filling
adds aroma and cuts any fishy taste; use a little to keep the chive flavour

jjajangmyeon.how: Use a nonstick pan to cook the pork belly until golden. Spoon off the extra fat, leaving a thin layer to cook the vegetables, and cook the onion until the edges are lightly golden. Push the meat and vegetables aside and stir the chunjang in the vegetable oil over medium-low heat. When you smell the paste, mix everything together and add the water, then the MSG. Cook through and thicken with a thin starch slurry. Stir in the sesame oil before turning off the heat.
notes: added when cooking the sauce, to make up for the savoury flavour lost with less meat

jok.how: Beat the ground meat to a fine, sticky paste following the original recipe, to keep the base flavour and tenderness of the meatballs. After the congee and meatballs are cooked, stir in the MSG, then taste and add salt. Keep the ginger, green onion and freshly ground white pepper to sprinkle on at serving, so the savoury flavour and spice stand out.
notes: stirred into the congee before serving to round out the savoury flavour; still use an unsalted stock

kalguksu.how: Knead the dough and cover it tightly. Rest it for half an hour, then roll and cut, keeping the noodles soft and chewy. Simmer the chicken stock over low heat until full, then skim off the fat, add the MSG and taste for salt. Keep the sesame oil to stir into the warm shredded chicken before filling the bowls, so the sesame aroma reaches the mouth directly.
notes: added to the chicken stock to round out the savoury flavour; taste for salt again at the end

kao-dan-ta.how: Add the vanilla and salt to the milk mixture, then stir in the egg yolks. Mix gently, strain and skim off any foam. Divide the filling evenly among the tart shells in the original recipe. Watch closely near the end of baking. Take the tarts out when the pastry is golden and the filling has just set but still trembles slightly, to keep them tender and avoid losing the milky flavour by overbaking.
notes: adds sweet aroma and brings out the egg and milk flavour
brings out the sweetness and milk flavour; it should not taste salty

kao-yu.how: Marinate the fish and pat the surface dry, then grill it until browned. Cook the green onion, garlic and whole spices until fragrant, then cook the base seasonings and doubanjiang until loosened. Bring the broth to a boil with the MSG. Sizzle the chilies and Sichuan pepper with off-heat hot oil in stages. Before serving, drizzle the vinegar down the side of the pan, then taste for salt. Do not cook it long, which concentrates the flavour.
notes: added down the side of the pan before serving, to add aroma and finish the flavour
added after the broth comes to a boil, to round out the savoury flavour

katsudon.how: Pat the pork cutlet dry and sprinkle with black pepper. Fry until the coating is golden, so the browned flavour adds seasoning. Cook the onion, covered, in unsalted dashi until soft. Then add the soy sauce, mirin, sugar and MSG. Simmer the cutlet briefly, then pour in the egg, keeping the sauce flowing. Pour it evenly over the cutlet and the rice on top when serving.
notes: added to the simmering liquid to round out the savoury flavour; still use unsalted kombu and bonito dashi

khao-man-gai.how: Cook the minced garlic in the chicken fat until pale golden before adding the rice, so the rice keeps a rich chicken flavour. Bring the dipping sauce to a boil and take it off the heat. Taste it with the chicken, so the ginger, garlic, chili and vinegar lift the fermented bean flavour. Add white pepper to the clear soup before serving, with no extra salt.
notes: divided between the chicken stock for the rice and the dipping sauce, to round out the savoury flavour
added to the clear soup before serving, for fragrance

khao-niao-mamuang.how: Steep the sweet coconut cream with the pandan leaf over low heat for fragrance, without cooking it long. Steam the sticky rice through and mix it in while hot. Cover to keep it warm so the sweet aroma goes into the grains. Cook the topping sauce until it thinly coats the back of a spoon and pour it right over the sticky rice when serving. Serve with ripe mango and toasted sesame seeds, for coconut flavour and a smooth texture.
notes: washed and tied in a knot, steeped while heating the coconut cream and removed before mixing with the rice

khao-soi.how: Still keep the coconut milk for frying the paste, as in the original steps. Cook it until thick first, then fry the paste until the fragrance fully opens. Add the remaining coconut milk and chicken stock together to braise the chicken. Once the chicken is cooked, stir in the starch slurry and simmer gently until the broth lightly coats the noodles. Taste last and add fish sauce. Serve each bowl with pickled mustard greens, raw shallot and lime.
notes: unsalted and skimmed of fat, to make up the volume and the savoury chicken flavour
a little of the water in the recipe, mixed into a slurry to bring back the way the broth coats the noodles

kitsune-udon.how: Simmer the fried tofu pouches over low heat and let them rest in the liquid so the sweet, salty flavour goes inside. They should stay moist when lifted. Heat the dashi, mirin and sugar for the broth first. Add the soy sauce and MSG just before filling the bowls, so the aroma is not lost to long cooking. Drain the noodles well and do not pour the tofu cooking liquid into the noodle broth.
notes: added to the broth for two servings, to round out the savoury flavour

kkakdugi.how: Salt and drain as in the original steps. First dissolve the MSG in the reserved radish liquid, then mix well with the chili, garlic, ginger and green onion, so the spicy flavour and umami cling to the cut surfaces. This version is a fresh radish cube kimchi for eating the same day. Refrigerate it below 4°C right after mixing. Do not follow the room-temperature fermenting and long storage steps.
notes: to make up for the savoury flavour lost with less fish sauce; it is not a substitute for the salt used in fermenting

kluay-buat-chi.how: Use a small pot in which the bananas fit snugly in one layer. First heat the pandan leaf gently in the coconut milk until fragrant, then add the bananas, sugar and salt. Return to a gentle simmer and cook briefly. Take it off the heat, cover and let it steep until the centre is soft, then uncover promptly. Do not cook it dry, which loses the coconut flavour.
notes: washed, bruised lightly and tied in a knot to add sweet aroma, removed before serving

kou-shui-ji.how: Cook the green onion, Sichuan pepper and garlic in oil over low heat until fragrant. Strain, then pour the oil over the pre-moistened chili flakes in stages, stirring as you pour and keeping the flakes whole. Cool, then stir in the chicken stock and the original seasonings. Taste with a piece of chicken and adjust the salty, sour and numbing heat. Pat the chicken dry before tossing it gently with the sauce, and top with crushed peanuts and cilantro.
notes: unsalted and skimmed of fat, cooled and used to make the sauce

kung-pao-chicken.how: Toast the peanuts in a dry pan over low heat until fragrant and set aside. In a nonstick pan, cook the dried chilies and Sichuan pepper over medium-low heat until fragrant. Turn the heat to high, add the diced chicken and break it up, then add the ginger, garlic and green onion whites and stir-fry quickly. Stir the bowl sauce before pouring it in and cook it to a thin glaze. Stir in the peanuts last and serve right away, to keep the Sichuan pepper aroma and the crunch.
notes: added to the bowl sauce to round out the savoury flavour

la-wei-bao-zai-fan.how: Lay the shredded ginger over the rice with the cured meats, so the ginger flavour and the fat from the cured meats seep into the rice. Take the pot off the heat once the rice crust smells toasty. While hot, pour over the soy sauce mixture and sprinkle with green onion. Toss well, so every bite is coated in cured-meat flavour and umami.
notes: cut into fine shreds and laid over the rice with the cured meats
stirred into the soy sauce mixture to round out the savoury flavour

lan-cai-rou-mo-si-ji-dou.how: In a nonstick pan, break up the ground pork over low heat. Render its own fat and cook off the juices, then cook until the edges turn slightly golden, and add the wine down the side of the pan. Briefly cook the garlic, preserved olive greens and chilies until fragrant. Add the beans and toss, then add hot water, cover and cook until the centre is soft. Uncover and reduce, so the savoury flavour coats the beans. Taste before serving and add salt.
notes: added down the side of the pan once the ground pork has golden edges; cook off the alcohol smell to add meaty flavour

lan-zhou-niu-rou-mian.how: Strain the broth and divide it among shallow containers. Cool quickly and refrigerate. Once the fat solidifies, remove it. Then cook the radish and reheat the beef, keeping the gelatin in the broth for a silky mouthfeel. Warm the chili oil over low heat and add the chili flakes to sizzle them, without burning. Spoon it over each bowl with cilantro and green onion tops, so the chili aroma is concentrated at first taste.
notes: a finely ground, unsalted chili flake, to replace the heat and chili aroma lost with less red oil

lao-you-zhu-rou-fen.how: Dry-fry the sour bamboo shoots until no water pools. Over medium-low heat, cook the garlic, roughly chopped fermented black beans, chopped pickled chilies and chili flakes until fragrant, then add the meat and water. Divide the light soy sauce between the meat marinade and the broth. Stir in the MSG once the noodles and meat are cooked. Taste the soup and finish with rice vinegar and white pepper. Add no more salt.
notes: pure chili flakes with no salt added, to make up for the heat and aroma
added after the soup is cooked, to round out the savoury flavour

lasagne-alla-bolognese.how: Cook the vegetables over medium-low heat until sweet and fragrant. Break up the beef, add the tomato paste and cook until fragrant. Then add the milk and wine and simmer slowly to reduce, as in the original steps. For the béchamel, cook the flour in the butter and olive oil and keep it pale. Dot the top evenly with butter and keep the original cheese to bake a thin crust. Taste the sauce for salt before assembling.
notes: used in the béchamel, to help disperse the flour along with the butter
used in the meat sauce; cook until fragrant before adding the milk

ma-la-qiao-mai-mian.how: First use the small amount of chili oil from the original recipe to cook the chili flakes and hot pot base over low heat until fragrant. Then add water and cook the noodles. Loosen the peanut butter first, add it with the milk and keep it at a gentle simmer. Off the heat, stir in the MSG and Sichuan pepper oil. Taste a little broth with the aged vinegar first, then add it in stages. Let umami, numbing aroma and sourness carry the flavour.
notes: pure chili flakes with no salt added, to make up for the heat and aroma
to add savoury flavour, instead of adding more light soy sauce

ma-la-xiang-guo.how: Drain the pre-cooked ingredients well and stir-fry in batches in a nonstick pan. Divide the frying oil, paste and spices evenly among the batches. Break up the paste over medium-low heat, then add the garlic, green Sichuan pepper and dried chilies. As soon as it smells fragrant, add the sliced meat and tofu sheets. Finally toss in the greens and noodles, so the sauce coats the ingredients evenly.
notes: minced, added when cooking the paste until fragrant
lightly crushed and briefly stir-fried with the dried chilies

mapo-tofu.how: Cook the ground meat until browned first. Over medium-low heat, cook the doubanjiang until it releases red oil, then cook the fermented black beans, chilies, ginger and garlic until fragrant. Use water for the base and add the MSG. Simmer the tofu gently so it takes up the flavour. Add the starch slurry in stages so the sauce coats the tofu. Sprinkle with freshly ground Sichuan pepper powder and eat while hot.
notes: added with the water to round out the savoury flavour

mien-ga.how: Roast the onion, ginger and shallot until they have brown spots and smell sweet. Remove the burnt parts before making the broth. After straining the broth, add the fish sauce and MSG. In each bowl, squeeze in lime and add freshly ground pepper. Add the fried shallots and cilantro leaves last, so umami, sour notes and onion aroma carry the flavour of this lower-salt soup.
notes: added after straining the broth, with the fish sauce, to round out the savoury flavour

moo-ping.how: Pound the garlic, cilantro stems and pepper into a wet paste. Toss with each slice in the marinade and chill for the full marinating time. Keep the fine bits of fat in the meat. Thread onto flat skewers. Grill first over the hot zone until browned, then move to a cooler zone. Take them off when the centre reaches 71°C (160°F) to keep the juices in.
notes: pounded fine with the cilantro stems and pepper in the recipe, for more garlic and grilled flavour
stirred into the marinade to round out the savoury flavour, without adding soy sauce

mousse-au-chocolat.how: Sift the cocoa powder first and mix it with warm strong coffee. Add the chocolate and melt it over a water bath. Off the heat, stir in the softened butter in stages. Stir the vanilla extract into the slightly warm chocolate base, then combine it with the egg yolk mixture. Gently fold in the whipped egg whites. Chill until fully set, to keep the fine bubbles and rich texture.
notes: unsweetened cocoa powder, to strengthen the chocolate flavour
vanilla extract, to bring out the chocolate and orange flavours

nikujaga.how: Add the ginger slices when stir-frying the beef. Once fragrant, add the vegetables and unsalted stock. When the potatoes are soft through, season in the original order. Add the MSG with the soy sauce, shake the pot gently and spoon the liquid over the ingredients. Taste for salt before serving. Keep a little cooking liquid, and let it rest briefly off the heat before serving.
notes: thinly sliced, for a fresh note that does not cover the stock flavour
to make up for the savoury flavour lost with less soy sauce

nong-jia-yi-wan-xiang.how: Use a nonstick pan. Cook the eggs just until set and remove them. Render the fat from the fatty pork first. Pat the lean meat dry, spread it in the pan and cook until the edges are light golden. Cook the ginger, garlic and doubanjiang until fragrant. Add the Shaoxing wine down the side of the pan and let the alcohol smell fade before returning the pepper and eggs. Finally add the MSG and toss gently, so the egg pieces coat in the meat juices.
notes: to remove any gamey taste and bring out the meat and doubanjiang flavours
to make up for the savoury flavour lost with less meat

oden.how: Use unsalted kombu and bonito dashi. Simmer the daikon over low heat until tender through, and add the fish cakes later, so their own salty, savoury flavour goes into the broth. Once the fish cakes are hot, stir in the MSG and taste the broth before serving. Serve the hot mustard in a separate dish for dipping, to lift the flavour with its pungency.
notes: added to the broth after the fish cakes are simmered, to round out the savoury flavour

ojingeo-bokkeum.how: Mix the MSG into the marinade first. When cooking the vegetables, let the edges of the onion brown slightly for a sweet aroma, then add the squid. Once the squid is cooked, add the rice vinegar and drizzle with sesame oil. Toss quickly and serve, to keep the aroma of the chili, garlic, ginger and sesame.
notes: unsalted and unsweetened rice vinegar, added before serving to brighten the sweet and spicy flavours
mixed into the sauce for the marinated squid, to round out the savoury flavour

okonomiyaki.how: Use a nonstick pan and brush on a thin layer of oil. Cut the pork belly into thin, long slices and lay them evenly over the pancake. After flipping, cook until browned and fragrant first, then turn the heat to low and cover. Uncover and cook off the steam from the surface. Brush with okonomiyaki sauce and drizzle with the mayonnaise thinned with vinegar. Just before serving, sprinkle with bonito flakes and green nori, to keep the umami and aroma.
notes: mixed into the mayonnaise, so it can be squeezed in fine lines over the pancake

omurice.how: Cook the onion until soft and sweet, then add the chicken and cook through. Cook the tomato paste and ketchup together until thick and fragrant, then mix with the rice. Mix the MSG into the rice and taste before serving. Season with black pepper for aroma. Divide the salt for the omelette into three parts and add it to the beaten eggs, to keep them tender. Drizzle with ketchup on the plate as usual.
notes: unsalted pure tomato paste, to make up for the rich tomato flavour
mixed into the whole pan of fried rice, to boost the chicken and tomato flavours

oyakodon.how: First dissolve the MSG and sugar in the dashi, then add the soy sauce. Add the chicken once it simmers gently, and never reduce the cooking liquid until thick. Add the green onion whites first and keep the tops to add before pouring in the egg. Once the chicken and the egg are each cooked to a safe doneness, put them in the bowl right away, to keep the green onion flavour and a tender texture.
notes: to round out the savoury flavour, paired with unsalted kombu and bonito dashi; it contains sodium, but the amount is small

pad-kee-mao.how: Add the pepper-garlic paste off the heat, then cook over medium heat until fragrant. Cook one portion at a time, so the sauce coats the rice noodles fully, and spread them out to sear briefly for browning. Still stir in the holy basil after turning off the heat and plate right away, to keep its spicy aroma.
notes: stirred into the sauce to make up for the savoury flavour lost with less sauce; divided evenly between the two pans

pad-kra-pao.how: Use a nonstick pan and divide the oil. First fry the egg until the edges are golden and the yolk has set, then use the remaining oil to cook the coarsely pounded garlic and chilies until fragrant. Add the ground meat and break it up. Cook off the water first, so some of the bits brown slightly. Add the original sauce and reduce to a thin, glossy coating on the meat. After turning off the heat, stir in the holy basil. Spoon it over hot rice as soon as the leaves wilt.

pad-pak-boong.how: Rinse and drain the fermented bean paste quickly. Bruise the garlic and chilies, then add them to the hot pan with the drained greens and stir-fry quickly until fragrant. As soon as the leaves are soft, add the unsalted chicken stock with the MSG dissolved in it. Keep a little of the light soy sauce, taste before serving and add it if needed. Remove the greens as soon as the stems are cooked, to keep the bean flavour and crispness.
notes: dissolved in the unsalted chicken stock to make up for the savoury flavour lost with less sauce

pad-prik-king.how: Use a nonstick pan and cook the meat in two batches. Add no oil at first, so the fat of the pork shoulder renders. Cook until brown spots form, then remove. Take the pan off the heat to cool slightly, then cook the curry paste in the leftover fat and vegetable oil until fragrant. If it sticks, add a little water at a time. Finally return the meat and reduce until the red sauce clings tightly to the meat and beans. Off the heat, stir in the finely shredded makrut lime leaves to keep the aroma.

pad-see-ew.how: Dissolve the palm sugar and MSG fully in the original sauce, and keep the sourness of the vinegar to lift the flavour. Still cook in two batches. First cook off the liquid at the bottom of the pan, then spread out the rice noodles and sear until browned and charred at the edges. Sprinkle with freshly ground white pepper at the end, so the toasty and spicy notes make up for the milder saltiness.
notes: stirred into the sauce to make up for the savoury flavour lost with less soy sauce
chopped and dissolved in the sauce to bring back the sweetness lost with less sweet dark soy sauce

pad-thai.how: Use a large nonstick pan. Use part of the oil to cook the shallot, garlic, preserved radish and dried shrimp until fragrant. Then cook the tofu and shrimp and set aside. Use the remaining oil to cook the noodles and toss with the sauce, adding water in stages if the pan is dry. Push the noodles aside to cook the egg, then combine with the other ingredients. When the shrimp are cooked and the noodles have no hard centre, add the bean sprouts. Off the heat, toss in the garlic chives and sprinkle with peanuts. Squeeze lime over it when eating.

panang-neua.how: Add water to the coconut milk to cover the whole piece of beef brisket. Simmer at a gentle bubble until the tendons are soft. Cook part of the thick coconut cream until the oil separates, add the vegetable oil and cook the curry paste until fragrant, then add the sugar and fish sauce. Stir in the peanut butter and the remaining coconut cream. Add the braising liquid in stages and reduce until it coats a spoon. You do not need to use all the braising liquid. Return the sliced meat to heat through. Finally stir in the makrut lime leaves and sweet basil, and taste for salt and sweetness before serving.
notes: unsweetened, unsalted smooth peanut butter made only of peanuts, to add protein, peanut flavour and a thick texture
a neutral vegetable oil such as canola, to help cook the curry paste until fragrant

parmigiana-di-melanzane.how: Salt the eggplant slices, then pat them dry. Coat them thinly in flour and shake off the extra. Brush both sides with oil and bake at high heat until golden and soft in the centre. Cook the minced garlic in olive oil until fragrant, add the tomato paste and cook briefly, then add the tomatoes and reduce. Taste and add salt. Drain the cheese well and spread it in thin slices. Layer and bake as in the original, keeping the browned flavour on top.
notes: to add rich tomato flavour and umami
finely minced, for the tomato sauce

petits-pois-a-la-francaise.how: When braising, use part butter and part canola oil. Cover tightly and keep at a gentle simmer. Add a little hot water when the pan is nearly dry. Once the vegetables are cooked, reduce the liquid until it is thin but slightly thick. Off the heat, stir in the reserved cold butter, so the liquid coats the peas. Finally taste and add salt.
notes: a mild canola oil, to make up for the richness while letting the butter and chervil aromas still come through

pho-bo.how: Roast the onion and ginger until sweet before adding them to the broth. Keep the bone broth at a gentle simmer, keeping a few droplets of fat. After straining, top up the broth, then add the MSG, fish sauce and salt. First taste the broth with the rice noodles. After filling the bowls, squeeze in lime juice and add herbs and freshly ground pepper to lift the flavour.
notes: added after the broth is strained and topped up, to round out the savoury flavour

pho-ga.how: Roast the ginger and onion until partly charred, then remove the burnt skin. Toast the coriander seeds until fragrant. Simmer the chicken carcass gently for the full time. Strain and top up the broth, add the MSG, then taste for salt. In each bowl, add the Thai basil and squeeze in lime juice, so fresh aroma and sourness lift the flavour.
notes: added to the strained broth to round out the savoury flavour of the chicken broth
torn and added to each bowl for a fresh herbal aroma

pi-dan-dou-fu.how: First stir the garlic, sugar and MSG into the vinegar and light soy sauce, then add the sesame oil and chili oil. Stir well before pouring. Drain the tofu and plate it just before eating. Spoon the sauce thinly over the tofu and preserved egg. Finally sprinkle with green onion, cilantro and crushed peanuts, so every bite has savoury flavour and crunch.
notes: minced fine, for more garlic flavour
dissolved in the sauce to round out the savoury flavour

pla-neung-manao.how: Dissolve the sugar in the chicken stock, then stir in the MSG. Off the heat, stir in the garlic, chilies, fish sauce and lime juice, to keep the fresh sourness and garlic aroma. Add the cilantro last. Pour the dressing into the cuts in the fish. When serving, spoon the juices from the bottom of the plate over the fish, so every bite is seasoned.
notes: to round out the savoury flavour, dissolved in the hot chicken stock; use an unsalted stock

pollo-alla-cacciatora.how: In a heavy-bottomed nonstick pan, cook the onion until soft and remove it. Brown the dried chicken pieces in batches until golden brown, pour off the extra fat and keep the browned bits in the pan. Return the onion and cook the tomato paste until fragrant. Deglaze with the white wine, scraping up the browned bits, then add the tomatoes and rosemary and simmer slowly. Remove the chicken when cooked, reduce the sauce, taste and add salt and black pepper, then return the chicken to coat.
notes: tomato paste with no added oil; cook until fragrant before adding the wine
fresh rosemary, added with the tomatoes and removed before serving

pot-au-feu.how: Dry-roast the cut side of the onion to a deep brown. Add the thyme in the herb bundle and keep the pot at a gentle simmer, so the connective tissue of the beef shoulder softens fully and leaves a gelatinous mouthfeel in the broth. After cooking, first remove the meat and vegetables. Chill the broth until the fat solidifies and remove it. Then reheat the meat and vegetables and taste for salt. Moisten the beef with hot broth and serve with Dijon mustard to lift the flavour.
notes: fresh thyme, added to the herb bundle
served with the beef, for dipping in small amounts

poulet-au-vinaigre.how: Pat the chicken skin dry and brown in batches until golden. Keep the browned bits at the bottom of the pan and pour off the extra fat. Deglaze with the vinegar and reduce well, then add strong chicken stock and thyme and braise the chicken, then add the cream. Remove the chicken when cooked and reduce the sauce until it thinly coats the back of a spoon. Stir in the juices from the plate, then taste and add salt and freshly ground black pepper before serving.
notes: a neutral vegetable oil, used with the butter for browning the chicken
fresh thyme, added with the chicken stock and removed before reducing

poulet-roti.how: Pat the chicken skin dry. Rub the chicken butter on the skin only, in a thin layer, and put thyme in the cavity. Baste only with the fat, using the roasting butter mixed with the vegetable oil from the recipe. For the sauce, skim off the fat and keep a little to soften the shallot. Use the chicken stock to scrape up the golden-brown pan juices and bits, add the white wine vinegar and reduce. Off the heat, stir in the finishing butter. Taste and add salt and black pepper before serving.
notes: fresh thyme, put in the cavity and removed after roasting
used in the pan sauce, added before reducing

profiteroles.how: First mix the cocoa powder with a little of the sauce water. Then cook with the chocolate over low heat until it thinly coats a spoon. Off the heat, stir in the cream and the finishing butter until glossy. Bake the puffs until deep golden and vent them to release steam. When fully cool, divide the ice cream evenly among the puffs. Just before serving, pour on the warm sauce, to keep the crisp shell, cold filling and rich chocolate flavour.
notes: unsweetened cocoa powder, to make up for the rich cocoa flavour of the chocolate sauce

puree-de-pommes-de-terre.how: Mash the potatoes fine while hot and let excess steam escape. Off the heat, stir in the softened butter in stages, then slowly stir in the canola oil until smooth. Add the nutmeg to the hot milk and stir the milk in in stages, until the purée is soft and holds a mound. Taste last and adjust with salt and white pepper. Serve right away on warm plates.
notes: a mild canola oil, to make up for the smooth texture while the butter flavour stays dominant
freshly grated, a pinch, to bring out the dairy flavour without covering the potato and butter

qi-shan-sao-zi-mian.how: Render the fat from the fatty pork over low heat, then add the lean meat and ginger. Simmer the meat until tender, turn the heat to the lowest setting and stir in the chili powder. Stop as soon as the oil turns red and smells fragrant. Brush a nonstick pan lightly with oil to cook the egg sheet. Cook the base vegetables until fragrant, then add a little water and steam until cooked. Keep adding the vinegar in stages when making the soup. Finally add the MSG and taste the soup for salt.
notes: added near the end of making the soup, to round out the savoury flavour

qie-zi-rou-jian-bing.how: Steam the eggplant slices until slightly soft and let the surface steam dry before coating in thin batter. Finely chop the cooked cured pork and mix with the green onion and white pepper, so every pancake has meaty flavour. Brush a nonstick pan with a thin layer of oil. Cook the pancakes in batches, flat, until golden on both sides, the centre is cooked and the cooked pork is reheated to 74°C (165°F). Taste a cooked pancake before serving and decide whether to add salt.
notes: sliced, mixed into the batter for fragrance
mixed into the batter, to bring out the cured pork flavour

qing-jiao-niang.how: Use a nonstick pan. Pat the green peppers dry and fry them in batches. First set the meat side, then fry the pepper skin until it has tiger-skin spots. Use the remaining oil in the pan to cook the garlic over low heat until fragrant, then add the sauce and braise until the filling is cooked through. At the end, uncover and reduce, and thicken lightly with a thin starch slurry, so the savoury flavour clings to the peppers. Taste the sauce before serving and decide whether to add salt.
notes: added to the braising sauce to round out the savoury flavour

quiche-lorraine.how: Keep the pastry cold while you work. Gather it into a ball only, and blind bake until the bottom is dry and lightly golden. Pat the bacon dry and fry lightly until fragrant, keeping it soft. Mix the mustard into the custard. Add a little salt in light of the saltiness of the bacon. Check early once the filling gets thin. Take it out as soon as the centre is cooked, to keep it tender.
notes: mixed into the custard to boost the flavour and bring out the bacon

rad-na.how: Cook the garlic and soybean paste over medium heat until fragrant, then add the unsalted stock and MSG. Still sear the rice noodles in two pans until browned in spots. Once the thickened sauce is cooked, taste it with the noodles. At the table, add a little chili vinegar to taste, so sour and spicy notes lift the flavour.
notes: added to the thickened stock, to make up for the savoury flavour lost with less salty sauce

ragu-napoletano.how: In a heavy-bottomed pot, brown the meat in batches. Use the leftover fat to slowly cook the onion. Add the red wine in stages and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom. If it gets dry, add a little hot water. Add the tomato paste in stages and cook until the colour deepens. When the meat is tender, remove it first, then reduce the sauce. Taste and add salt before serving.

ravioli-ricotta-spinaci.how: Melt the butter over low heat. Add the sage and simmer until fragrant, then add the olive oil, taking care not to brown the butter. After lifting the ravioli into the pan, add a little of the cooking water at a time. Off the heat, shake the pan gently until a thin sauce coats the pasta evenly. Taste for salt before plating.
notes: mixed with the butter to make the sage sauce, to keep a silky texture

risotto-alla-milanese.how: Cook the onion over medium-low heat until completely soft, so the bone marrow melts into the fat. Add the rice and cook until glossy. Cook the white wine until the sharp smell of alcohol fades. Once the rice is cooked, leave plenty of flowing, thick liquid. Off the heat, stir in the cold butter and finely grated cheese. Shake the pan gently so the fat blends with the starchy liquid. Taste last and add salt, then plate on warm plates right away.
notes: added to the pot with the butter and beef marrow used to cook the onion; choose a mild-flavoured olive oil

rou-dan-gai-fan.how: Use a nonstick skillet. Spread the ground meat thin and brown the bottom before turning. When the meat is cooked, push it to one side and use the rendered fat to cook the minced shallot until fragrant. Leave a space and crack in the eggs. Add the bowl sauce and cook over low heat until the eggs are cooked through. If the pan is nearly dry, add a little hot water, to keep a rich sauce for mixing with the rice.
notes: finely minced and cooked until fragrant, to bring back the shallot aroma
added to the bowl sauce, for fragrance

rou-jia-mo.how: Still use a small pot to braise the skin-on pork until the skin is soft and the meat is tender. Lift it out and skim the fat from the surface of the braising liquid, then uncover and reduce slightly. Chop the meat into small pieces and mix with the MSG and the defatted braising liquid, keeping it moist without pooling liquid. Fill the buns while the meat and buns are both hot.
notes: added when mixing the meat filling, to round out the savoury flavour

salade-lyonnaise.how: Toss the bread cubes in a thin coat of oil and bake spread out until golden and crisp. Fry the bacon until crisp, remove and drain. Leave only a thin layer of fat in the pan to cook the shallot until fragrant. Use the red wine vinegar to scrape up the browned bits, then whisk with the mustard and olive oil. Add no more oil. Just before serving, toss in the spun-dry frisée. Top with the hot ingredients and the poached egg, so the runny yolk adds a silky texture.
notes: minced, used in the warm vinaigrette

saltimbocca-alla-romana.how: Use a nonstick pan and sear quickly in batches in olive oil. The meat side does most of the cooking, and the ham side only needs a dozen seconds, to keep the juices and ham flavour. Remove the meat and turn the heat to low. Add the butter and shake the pan to blend with the unburnt juices, then pour it back over right away, so the butter and sage aroma gather on the surface.
notes: used for searing the meat in batches; keep the butter to add aroma at the end

san-bei-ji.how: Use a nonstick pan. Start the chicken pieces skin side down until lightly golden and pour off the extra rendered fat. Add the lard, ginger, garlic and green onion whites and cook over low heat until fragrant, then pour in the braising sauce. Cover and braise until cooked, then uncover and reduce. When the sauce just coats the chicken, add the green onion tops and sesame oil, toss and plate right away.
notes: sesame oil, added before serving for aroma

satay-gai.how: Still divide the marinade and the coconut milk for brushing evenly. Mix the lemongrass and garlic paste into the marinade. Brush thinly and turn while grilling, so the surface chars. Cook the red curry paste in the oil from the recipe with a little coconut milk first, then add the other sauce ingredients. Add the water in stages until the sauce coats a skewer, then turn off the heat. Toss the cucumber with the vinegar dressing just before serving, to keep it crisp, sweet and sour.
notes: tender core only, finely chopped and added to the chicken marinade
mashed to a paste and added to the chicken marinade

sha-zhu-cai.how: Rinse the pickled cabbage briefly and squeeze it dry. Cook the ribs until slightly golden, then add the pickled cabbage and cook until the sour smell comes up, then add water and stew. When adding the blood sausage, sprinkle with white pepper. Add the MSG before serving to boost the savoury flavour. Mix the dipping sauce from garlic paste, chili oil and sesame oil, and dip lightly.
notes: added before serving, to round out the savoury flavour
added with the blood sausage, for fragrance

shan-bei-ao-dou-jiao.how: Cook the green beans and potatoes through first, then add the tomatoes and the original seasonings. Cook until the tomatoes break down and a layer of thick sauce remains at the bottom. Just before serving, add the extra garlic for flavour and cook briefly until fragrant, then stir in the MSG. Taste the potatoes with the thick sauce, then add the reserved salt in stages.
notes: added after the sauce is reduced, to round out the savoury flavour
extra for flavour, minced and added just before serving

shan-xi-guo-you-rou.how: Divide the light soy sauce between the coating and the final stir-fry. Cook the green onion, ginger and garlic until fragrant before adding the vegetables. When the sliced meat returns to the pan, stir in the MSG and reduce to a thin sauce that coats the ingredients. Taste a cooked vegetable before serving and add no more salt. Drizzle the aged vinegar down the side of the pan, toss and plate right away, to keep the vinegar and Sichuan pepper aroma.
notes: added when the sliced meat returns to the pan, to round out the savoury flavour

shan-xi-you-po-mian.how: Pile the green onion and garlic on the noodles and spread the chili powder in a thin layer. Heat the oil until fine ripples appear but it does not smoke.
