Pour it over the seasonings in stages, then toss right away. After pouring the oil, add a little hot noodle water to help the seasoning coat the noodles. Taste last and add salt, then eat while hot.
notes: dissolved in the light soy sauce and black vinegar, to round out the savoury flavour

shou-rou-tu-dou-pian.how: Marinate the sliced pork with the shredded ginger. Add the meat to a hot pan and spread it out, then stir-fry once the surface has set. Add the garlic and the white parts of the garlic shoots and cook until fragrant, then add the drained potatoes and the other seasonings. Taste before serving and add the reserved salt a little at a time.
notes: cut into fine shreds and marinated with the sliced meat
minced and cooked with the white parts of the garlic shoots until fragrant

shou-si-bao-cai.how: Use a nonstick pan. First cook the pork belly until cooked through and the edges are lightly golden, then remove it. Use the rendered fat to cook the ginger, garlic and bird's eye chilies until fragrant. Drain the cabbage well. Stir-fry it quickly in batches in the vegetable oil and the lard in the pan, and combine with the meat when the leaves are soft and the stems crisp. Toss with the light soy sauce, cooking wine and chicken bouillon. Just before serving, add the black vinegar and garlic shoots, taste for salt and plate promptly.

shoyu-ramen.how: Still cook the chashu in the broth first and then in the soy sauce liquid. Slice it thin and spread out, so every bite has pork flavour. Before filling the bowls, cook a small amount of minced leek whites in vegetable oil over low heat until fragrant, and divide the oil with the leek among the bowls. Add the MSG to the bone broth. Taste for salt again after combining in the bowl, to keep the original gelatinous, silky texture.
notes: a neutral vegetable oil, used to cook a small amount of minced leek whites; divided among eight bowls
dissolved in the unsalted bone broth before filling the bowls, to round out the savoury flavour

shui-zhu-rou-pian.how: Marinate the meat with only a little oil to seal the coating. Stir-fry the side vegetables in a nonstick pan. Cook the cut chilies over low heat until crisp and take them off as soon as they smell fragrant. For the broth, first cook the ginger, garlic, pickled chilies and doubanjiang in oil until fragrant, then add water and cook until flavourful. Taste for salt before serving. Pile the cut chilies, garlic and green onion in the centre of the meat. Pour a thin stream of hot oil over them, to release the aroma fully.

sole-meuniere.how: Pat the fish dry and dredge it thinly in flour just before it goes in the pan. In a nonstick pan, heat the canola oil first, then add the butter for cooking the fish. Cook over medium heat until a thin golden crust forms. Cook the finishing butter separately in a clean small pan until light brown flecks appear and it smells nutty, then take it off the heat right away. Drizzle the fish with lemon juice in stages and sprinkle with parsley. Pour on the hazelnut-coloured butter and serve hot.
notes: a mild canola oil, used with the butter for cooking the fish; split evenly between the pans

souffle-au-fromage.how: Still keep part of the butter for greasing the mould. Cook the flour in the rest of the butter and olive oil, keeping it pale, then add hot milk and cook until a spoon leaves a trail on the bottom of the pot. Off the heat, stir in the mustard and egg yolks. Grate the cheese finely, keeping the part for coating the mould and sprinkling on top, so the baked flavour stands out. Use the original number of egg whites and fold gently. Serve right away after baking.
notes: a mild one, used with the butter for the béchamel to cook the flour
stirred in off the heat after the béchamel, to lift the cheese flavour

spaghetti-allamatriciana.how: Slowly render the guanciale over medium-low heat and remove it when the edges are golden. Use the fat in the pan to cook the tomato paste until fragrant, then pour in the white wine, scraping up the bottom of the pan, and add the tomatoes and reduce. After adding the pasta, add a little pasta water and toss well. Off the heat, stir in the finely grated pecorino in batches. Taste with the pasta and add salt.
notes: a small amount, to make up for the concentration and savoury flavour of the tomato

steak-au-poivre.how: Pat the steak dry and sear it to a brown crust. Keep the browned bits that have not burnt. Scrape them up with the stock and reduce, then add the cognac and cook off the sharp smell of alcohol. While the liquid is still flowing, stir in the Dijon mustard. Off the heat, shake in the cold butter in stages to make a thin, glossy sauce. Finally mix in the juices released while the steak rests, then taste and add salt.
notes: plain Dijon mustard, to help emulsify the pan juices and lift the flavour without covering the black pepper and cognac

steamed-fish.how: First sizzle the shredded ginger in hot oil, then pour in the soy sauce mixture and bring to a boil. Finally add the shredded green onion whites, to keep the bright ginger and green onion aroma. Pour off all the steaming liquid before spooning on the sauce, so the seasoning clings to the fish. Dip the fish in a little of the sauce from the bottom of the plate as you eat.
notes: added to the soy sauce mixture to round out the savoury flavour

suan-cai-yu.how: Taste the pickled mustard greens before rinsing, and soak briefly only if they are harshly salty. Cook them until the sour aroma comes up, fry the fish bones until fragrant, then make the broth. Remove the fish bones and add the MSG. After the fish slices are cooked, finish the sourness with the rice vinegar and taste for salt. Keep the final pour of sizzling oil over the ginger, garlic, Sichuan pepper and chilies.
notes: unsalted rice vinegar, added in stages to taste for sourness after the fish slices are cooked
added to the broth after the fish bones are removed, to round out the savoury flavour

suan-dou-jiao-rou-mo.how: Dice the pickled long beans, rinse quickly, drain and pat off the surface water. Spread the ground meat in the pan and break it up, cooking until the edges are lightly golden. Use the oil in the pan to cook the green onion whites, ginger, garlic and doubanjiang until fragrant. Once the beans are hot, drizzle the rice vinegar down the side of the pan and sprinkle with the green onion tops. Taste a bite with the meat before serving. Add no more salt.
notes: unsalted rice vinegar, added before serving for a sour aroma
whites and tops chopped separately

suan-la-fen.how: First mix the garlic paste, vinegar, chili oil and Sichuan pepper powder in the bottom of the bowl. Pour in the hot broth and add the MSG, so the sour, spicy and numbing flavours spread fully. Slice the zha cai thin and sprinkle it evenly over each bowl. Finally add the peanuts and green onion. After mixing, taste the soup again and finish with vinegar and Sichuan pepper. Do not add salt based on the first taste.
notes: total for two servings, to make up for the savoury flavour lost with less light soy sauce
extra garlic, mashed to a paste to strengthen the garlic flavour

suan-ni-bai-rou.how: Toast the chili flakes in a dry pan over low heat until fragrant and moisten them with the reserved meat broth. Let cool until warm, then stir in the garlic paste, which has been mashed fine and rested, the prepared soy sauce and the other seasonings. Keep part of the red oil to spoon over at the end. Slice the meat thin against the grain and spread it out, so every slice is coated on both sides in the garlicky, spicy sauce.
notes: a fragrant, spicy fine chili flake, to make up for the heat and chili aroma lost with less red oil
stirred into the garlic sauce to round out the savoury flavour

sukiyaki.how: In step 2, dissolve the MSG in the warishita. In step 4, first cook part of the green onion and shiitake in oil until fragrant, then add the warishita and cook the beef. Take the meat out as soon as it is cooked. After that, keep a shallow broth so the ingredients coat in the sweet, salty, savoury flavour. When the liquid evaporates, add kombu water first and taste the ingredients before deciding whether to add more warishita.
notes: added to the warishita to round out the savoury flavour

sundubu-jjigae.how: Cut the pork belly into small pieces and cook it in a nonstick pan until the fat renders. Cook the garlic, onion and sour kimchi until fragrant, adding a little stock if it sticks. Loosen the chili powder with a little stock and vegetable oil and add it to the pot with the rest of the stock, so it does not turn bitter from dry-frying. Once the tofu is hot, add the MSG, taste and add salt. Keep the sesame oil to drizzle on just before serving.
notes: to make up for the savoury flavour of the broth, added once the tofu is hot

tai-shi-lu-rou-fan.how: Use a nonstick pan and cook the meat over medium heat. Keep a little of the rendered fat to cook the shallot until fragrant, then add the garlic and sugar, taking care not to burn them. Add the ginger slices and the original seasonings and braise gently until the skin is soft and tender. Finally stir in the MSG. Stop when the braising liquid thinly coats the back of a spoon, leaving plenty of sauce for the rice.
notes: thinly sliced, added with the whole spices and removed before reducing
stirred in after the reduction, to round out the meaty flavour

tai-shi-niu-rou-mian.how: Cook the green onion, onion, ginger and garlic until the edges are lightly golden. Then over medium-low heat, cook the doubanjiang until it releases red oil and the tomato paste until fragrant, and add the wine promptly to scrape up the bottom of the pan. Rinse and squeeze the pickled mustard greens, and cook until no water pools. Once the beef broth is hot, stir in the MSG. In each bowl, add rice vinegar and sprinkle with green onion. Taste and add no extra salt.
notes: added once the beef broth is hot, to round out the savoury flavour
divided among the bowls when filling them, to lift the aroma and finish the flavour

tang-mian.how: Top up the stock with water to the original volume. First cook the ginger slices and shiitake gently until fragrant, then add the tofu and greens. Cook the noodles in a separate pot, drain and put them in the bowls. Keep the light soy sauce to add just before serving, taste, and finish with white pepper. Add no extra salt. Off the heat, add a few drops of sesame oil and sprinkle with green onion.
notes: thinly sliced, cooked with the shiitake until fragrant
sliced, sprinkled on before serving

tarte-tatin.how: Spread the softened butter evenly over the bottom and sides of the pan. Drizzle the melted butter over in three additions, evenly, so every layer of apples is coated. Add the vanilla extract when tossing the apples with the sugar. Bake until the sugar syrup at the edges is thick and brown, so the caramel flavour develops fully. Once the pastry has enough colour, cover with foil and keep baking.
notes: added with the sugar when tossing the apples, to bring out the apple and caramel flavours

thit-kho-trung.how: Marinate the minced shallot with the pork. Keep part of the fish sauce to add near the end of the reduction, to keep its savoury aroma. Add the MSG once the skin is soft from braising. Keep the braising liquid flowing and rest it for a few minutes before tasting, so it does not reduce too thick.
notes: minced, added to the pork marinade for onion and sweet aroma
added near the end of the reduction, to round out the savoury flavour

tiramisu.how: Beat the egg yolks and sugar until thick enough to leave a trail, then stir in the vanilla extract. Mix in the cold cheese in batches at low speed. Stop as soon as it is smooth. Dip the ladyfingers quickly in strong coffee. Spread the cheese cream in two thin layers, chill until set and then dust with cocoa, so the coffee and cocoa flavours stand out.
notes: unsweetened vanilla extract, mixed into the yolk mixture to bring out the cheese and coffee flavours

tom-kha-gai.how: First simmer the thinly sliced, bruised galangal, lemongrass and makrut lime leaves in the chicken stock. Once fragrant, add the coconut milk, chicken, mushrooms and fish sauce. Keep at a gentle bubble. When the chicken is nearly done, stir in the starch slurry and cook gently until the broth is slightly thick, the mushrooms are tender and the centre of the chicken reaches 74°C (165°F). Off the heat, stir in the lime juice and chilies. Taste the broth with a mushroom, adjust the sourness and saltiness slightly, and sprinkle with cilantro.
notes: mixed with 115 ml cold water, to make up the volume and add a smooth texture

tom-saep.how: Still add the lemongrass, galangal and lime leaves in the second half of the simmer. Toast the dried chilies until fragrant before pounding. Once the vegetables are cooked, stir in the fish sauce and MSG, and add the lime juice off the heat. Just before serving, add the toasted rice powder and fresh herbs. Taste the meat and broth together, so sour, spicy, savoury and toasted rice flavours finish together.
notes: added with the fish sauce, to round out the savoury flavour
fresh mint leaves, torn and added just before serving

tom-yum-goong.how: Cook the peeled shrimp heads and shells with the bruised lemongrass, galangal and torn lime leaves. Once the savoury aroma comes out, remove the shells. Then cook the vegetables, add the fish sauce and MSG, and add the shrimp last. Off the heat, add the lime juice and cilantro. Taste and adjust the sour and spicy notes with a little lime juice or bruised chilies, so the shrimp flavour and spice aroma stand out.
notes: added with the fish sauce, to round out the savoury flavour

tomato-egg.how: Use a nonstick pan and divide the oil in two. Use a bit more for the eggs and a bit less for the tomatoes. After adding the eggs, push them gently into large curds and remove them while the surface is still moist. Add the tomatoes with their juices, press some of the flesh lightly and reduce. Taste for salt before returning the eggs. Toss to coat and heat through, then serve, to keep the sour aroma and tenderness.

tortellini-in-brodo.how: Brown the pork until golden before grinding it for the filling. Grate the cheese finely, mix it well with the nutmeg and chill overnight. Top up the two clear broths with water to the original volume and add the MSG. Cook the tortellini directly in the broth, so the savoury flavour of the filling goes into the soup. Add black pepper before serving, taste, and add no salt or extra cheese.
notes: added to the clear broth to make up for the savoury flavour lost when it was diluted
freshly ground and added before serving, without covering the nutmeg aroma

tu-dou-dun-pai-gu.how: Use a nonstick pan. Cook the sugar with a little water until reddish brown, then add the dried ribs and toss to coat. Then cook the ginger, garlic and spices in oil until fragrant, and add the wine, sauce and hot water and braise. Skim off the fat before adding the potatoes. Near the end of the reduction, drizzle the vinegar down the side of the pan, taste, and add salt in stages. Shake the pan gently so the thick sauce coats the ingredients.
notes: bruised, cooked with the ginger slices until fragrant
drizzled down the side of the pan near the end of the reduction, to add aroma without a sour taste

wei-bo-cong-jiang-hei-xue-yu.how: Drain the pooled liquid from the cooked fish and spoon on the light soy sauce and sesame oil. Pile the drained shredded green onion and ginger in the centre of the fish. Heat the oil for pouring in a small pot, take it off the heat, and spoon it over the green onion and ginger to sizzle them. Then toss the green onion, ginger and sauce together and serve right away.

wu-gu-ji-zhao.how: First mix the garlic and bird's eye chilies with the vinegar, sugar and MSG, then add the other seasonings. Add the lemon juice in stages, tasting as you go, so it is not so sour that it covers the savoury flavour. Drain the chicken feet well and toss with the sauce. Chill to let them take on the flavour, turning them partway through. Toss again before eating, so the garlic, numbing heat and savoury flavour coat evenly.
notes: dissolved in the dressing to make up for the savoury flavour lost with less sauce

xi-hong-shi-ji-dan-gua-mian.how: Cook the green onion whites and garlic until fragrant, then add the tomato paste and cook until fragrant, then add the tomatoes. Cook until soft and juicy, and reduce until the sauce coats the noodles. Cook the dried noodles in plain water, drain and toss with the sauce. Do not add any cooking water. Finally stir in the MSG, green onion tops and sesame oil. Taste the whole bowl and add no extra salt.
notes: unsalted pure tomato paste, to make up for the rich tomato flavour and umami
stirred in before serving to add savoury flavour with little added sodium

xian-rou-cai-fan.how: Start the cured pork in a cold pan with the vegetable oil and part of the lard. Cook until the fat turns slightly translucent and the edges are lightly golden, then add the green onion whites and cook until fragrant. Then cook the bamboo shoots and greens stems as in the original steps. When the rice is cooked, gently fluff it with the reserved lard, green onion tops and white pepper, so the meat and green onion flavours coat each grain evenly.
notes: canola oil or another oil lower in saturated fat, used for cooking the ingredients
whites minced and cooked until fragrant; tops minced and kept to stir into the rice

xian-rou-shao-mai.how: Add the salt, light soy sauce and MSG to the cold ground meat. Stir hard in one direction until sticky, then beat in the stock in stages, letting each addition be fully absorbed before adding more. Finely chop the shiitake and mix well with the ginger and green onion. Add the sesame oil last. Steam until the centre reaches a safe temperature and take them out, to keep the juices and aroma.
notes: mixed into the meat filling with the light soy sauce, to round out the savoury flavour

xian-rou-xiao-hun-tun.how: Keep the bone broth at a light simmer until the bone and meat flavour is fully released. Strain until clear, then add the salt and MSG. Mix the ground meat with the salt and light soy sauce until sticky, then beat in the cold water in stages. Put the green onion, white pepper and sesame oil in the bottom of the bowls and pour in the hot broth just before serving to bring out the aroma.
notes: added to the strained clear broth to round out the savoury flavour; total for four servings

xiang-cun-pi-jiu-ya.how: Drain the duck pieces well. In a nonstick pan, start them skin side down over medium-low heat to render the fat and pour off the extra. Use the thin layer of fat left in the pan to cook the Sichuan pepper and the other spices until fragrant, and pour in the beer as soon as you smell them. Braise. When the meat is tender, uncover and reduce, so the flavour coats the duck. Finally add the MSG, garlic shoots and green onion, and taste for salt before serving.
notes: added at the end, to round out the savoury flavour

xiang-gu-hua-ji.how: Pat the chicken dry and spread it in the pan to brown in light golden patches. Cook the green onion, ginger, garlic and shiitake until fragrant, then add the strained soaking water and MSG and cook briefly. Keep part of the light soy sauce to add near the end of the reduction. When the chicken is cooked through and the sauce thinly coats it, add the white pepper, drizzle with sesame oil and sprinkle with green onion. Turn off the heat right away, so it does not reduce dry.
notes: added to the cooking liquid to round out the savoury flavour of the chicken and shiitake
added before serving, for fragrance without covering the mushroom flavour

xiao-ji-dun-mo-gu.how: Pat the chicken dry and brown in batches in a nonstick pan, skin side down first to render the fat. Remove once browned and pour off the extra fat. In the same pan, cook the green onion, ginger and star anise until fragrant. Scrape up the browned bits with the clarified mushroom soaking water, then return the chicken and braise. Finally reduce to a thin sauce that coats the chicken, stir in the white pepper and green onion tops, taste and decide whether to add salt.
notes: added before serving, to bring out the savoury flavour of the chicken and shiitake

xin-jiang-da-pan-ji.how: Use a nonstick pan and cook the sugar over low heat. As soon as it turns amber, add the dried chicken pieces and toss until coloured. Then add the ginger, garlic and spices and add the seasoning liquid once you smell them. After braising, gently reduce until the sauce coats the chicken and potatoes. Keep plenty of liquid for the noodles. Taste for salt before serving.
notes: sliced, added to the pan with the garlic and spices for more spicy aroma

yaki-gyoza.how: Add the MSG with the seasonings for the filling and mix the ground meat until sticky, then mix in the squeezed-dry cabbage. Mix the dipping sauce and dip only the side of the dumplings lightly, so the vinegar lifts the flavour. Before serving, cook off all the water and sear the bottom until crisp, so the browned flavour and sesame oil aroma come through fully.
notes: added to the meat filling to make up for the savoury flavour lost with less soy sauce

yakisoba.how: Use a nonstick pan. Add a little water to the cooked noodles, cover and heat until loosened. Uncover and cook off the liquid, then remove. Cook the pork belly in batches until the edges are light brown. Use the rendered fat to cook the vegetables, keeping the browned bits in the pan. Finally return the meat, vegetables and noodles in batches. Drizzle the sauce down the side of the pan, toss quickly until dry, and serve sprinkled with green nori and with red pickled ginger.
notes: dissolved in the sauce actually used for the noodles, to round out the savoury flavour

yakitori.how: Reduce the glaze until it thinly coats the back of a spoon. Do not stop at the original remaining volume. Then divide it into one portion for brushing and one for finishing. Grill the chicken first until browned and fragrant, then brush on the sauce thinly in stages. Stir the yuzu juice into the finishing glaze off the heat. Brush it on with a clean brush when plating, so the savoury flavour and fresh citrus aroma stay on the surface.
notes: thinly sliced, simmered with the green onion tops in the glaze and removed after cooking
unsalted yuzu juice, stirred into the glaze kept for finishing

yam-khai-dao.how: First pound the garlic and chilies fine, then add the sugar and pound until blended. Add the lime juice, fish sauce and MSG for a dressing with clear sour and spicy notes. Drain the vegetables well. Drain the oil from the fried eggs and toss with the dressing just before eating. Taste a full bite with the egg pieces, so each piece has a thin coat of the dressing.
notes: peeled and pounded fine with the chilies, for more spicy aroma
dissolved in the dressing to make up for the savoury flavour lost with less fish sauce

yang-cong-chao-zhu-rou.how: Use a nonstick pan and spread the oil evenly over the bottom. Pat the sliced pork dry and cook in batches. As soon as it browns slightly, add the garlic and cook until fragrant, then remove it. Soften the onion in the fat left in the pan, adding a little water if it sticks. Once it is dry, add the sauce. Return the meat, cook through and reduce until the sauce thinly coats it. Off the heat, stir in the sesame oil, taste, and plate.

yang-pai-men-mian.how: Drain the lamb chops well. In a nonstick pan, cook the sugar into caramel and stir-fry the lamb. Add the ginger and garlic and cook until fragrant, then add the cooking wine down the side of the pan. After braising until tender, skim off the fat and keep enough lamb broth to braise the noodles. When the noodles are cooked, reduce briefly so the thick broth coats the noodle sheets. Taste the broth and adjust the salt before serving.
notes: bruised and added to the pan with the ginger to cook until fragrant, for more meaty flavour
added down the side of the pan after the lamb is fragrant, then add water and braise

yang-zhi-gan-lu.how: Stir the coconut milk until smooth. Soak the seeds in part of the coconut milk and all of the milk. After 10 minutes, break up any clumps and stir again. Chill until the seeds have fully absorbed the liquid. Choose very ripe mango. Blend the part for puréeing with the remaining coconut milk until fine. Stop the blender and scrape down the sides, then blend briefly again, so the purée makes up for a thicker texture. Peel the grapefruit and remove all the white pith. Fold the segments in last, to keep the fresh fruit flavour.

yang-zhou-chao-fan.how: Use a nonstick pan. Cook the eggs until just set and remove them. Cook the luncheon meat until the edges are lightly golden and use the rendered fat to cook the green onion whites until fragrant. Loosen the cold rice first and drain the other ingredients well. Stir-fry in batches until dry and separate, then toss the eggs and other ingredients back in. Add the white pepper and MSG. Taste with the meat before serving and add salt.
notes: added when the ingredients return to the pan, for fragrance without covering the egg and shrimp flavours
stirred in last to round out the savoury flavour; taste before deciding whether to add salt

yangnyeom-chicken.how: Cook the garlic until pale golden, then add the tomato paste and cook over low heat until fragrant. Add the other sauce ingredients and the Korean chili powder and stir over heat until blended and thick. Cool the twice-fried wings on a rack to let the steam escape. As soon as the sauce is bubbling again, turn off the heat and toss the wings in a thin coat, quickly, so the garlic, sweet heat and tang sit on the surface.
notes: unsalted pure tomato paste, to make up for the rich tomato flavour and body of the sauce
unsalted Korean chili powder, to add heat, aroma and red colour

you-men-da-xia.how: Cook the green onion, ginger and Sichuan pepper over low heat until fragrant. When searing the shrimp, press the heads lightly so the tomalley melts into the sauce. Remove the cooked shrimp first. Reduce the sauce on its own until it thinly coats the back of a spoon, then stir in the salt, MSG and rice vinegar. Taste, add the reserved flavoured oil and spoon it evenly back over the shrimp.
notes: added when the reduction is nearly done, to round out the savoury flavour of the shrimp juices
added before serving, to lift the flavour without a sour taste

yukgaejang.how: In step 6, sizzle the chili in warm sesame oil as in the original, to bring out its aroma. Keep the salt for last. Measure the base broth to the exact volume in the recipe. Cook the green onion until soft and sweet, then add the MSG. Then add the reduced amount of salt in stages, tasting as you go. Add no extra salt.
notes: to make up for the savoury flavour of the beef, shiitake and soup soy sauce; dissolved in the soup before serving

yun-tun-mian.how: Stir the salt into the pork until sticky, then beat in the filling water in stages. Finally mix in the diced shrimp. Gently cook the ginger slices in the chicken stock until fragrant and remove them. Before taking it off the heat, add the MSG and the white pepper from the recipe. Taste for savoury flavour before deciding whether to add salt. Cook the noodles and wontons in plain water, drain well and divide among six bowls. Pour in the hot broth, sprinkle with green onion and eat right away.
notes: thinly sliced, cooked in the broth for fragrance and removed
added to the chicken stock before taking it off the heat, to round out the savoury flavour

zha-jiang-mian.how: Use a nonstick pan and break up the ground meat. When there is less steam and it smells slightly browned, add the green onion and ginger, then add the wine down the side of the pan and cook until fragrant. Add the two pastes and keep stirring over low heat. If it gets too dry, add a little water, and cook until thick enough to coat the spatula. Drain the noodles well before tossing with the sauce, to keep the sauce flavour and cling.
notes: minced fine, added to the pan with the green onion for more aroma
drizzled down the side of the pan after the meat is cooked; cook until the alcohol smell fades

zheng-lu-mian.how: Use a nonstick pan and spread out the sliced meat. Cook over medium heat until the edges are lightly golden, then use the rendered fat to cook the green onion, ginger, garlic and dried spices until fragrant. After braising, add the MSG, taste the sauce and decide whether to add salt. Toss with the noodles in stages, so every noodle is coated in the meaty sauce, then steam again.
notes: added to the braising liquid before tossing with the noodles, to make up for the savoury flavour lost with less meat

zi-bo-shao-kao.how: Chop the fermented black beans and mix them into the sesame sweet bean sauce. Taste first and add no salt. Cook the skewers first over a gentler spot, then move to a hotter spot to brown. Near the end, sprinkle thinly with cumin. Cut the meat into small pieces and divide evenly among the small flatbreads, so every bite has meat, green onion and sauce.
notes: chopped, a small amount to add savoury flavour without covering the sesame and grilled meat flavours
ground cumin, sprinkled thinly near the end of grilling for aroma

zi-ran-niu-rou.how: Pat the beef dry and coat it. Spread it in a hot pan and cook until browned and fragrant. Cook the garlic with the green onion until fragrant. Add the cumin in stages, and add the drained green peppers as soon as you smell it. When the beef is cooked, add the MSG and toss. Taste before serving and add more cumin for aroma. Add no extra salt, and plate promptly.
notes: minced, cooked with the green onion until fragrant
added before serving, to round out the savoury flavour

zui-pai-gu.how: Pat the ribs dry and toss them into a thin batter that clings to the meat. Brush the surface lightly with oil. Cook in an air fryer preheated to 200°C (400°F), turning the ribs, until the crust is crisp and the centre reaches 71°C (160°F). Mix the drunken sauce ahead and sizzle the garlic in a little hot oil to release its aroma. Toss the hot ribs in a thin coat of the sauce right out of the fryer, spread them on a plate and eat while hot.
notes: added when marinating the ribs, for fragrance without covering the sweet, sour and garlic notes of the sauce
